Thank you all for raising these issues — this is exactly why we do the pre-filing review. Let me summarize what I'm hearing and what I need before I can give final approval.

First, Elias, you've identified prior art that defeats our broad system claim, but you have a workable narrower claim scope — 'on-device inference using a locally maintained model cache synchronized through an intermittent gateway.' I'll need that narrowed claim language incorporated into the nonprovisional application draft.

Second, Nina, the university sponsored-research agreement requires us to send an option notice within 20 business days before any non-U.S. filing. That needs to be added to the IP docket immediately, and we need to build that into our timeline.

Third, Owen, the export-control classification means we need a technology-control plan in place before any foreign filing or disclosure. That also has to go into the patent approval packet.

So the picture is: we can proceed with filing the nonprovisional with the narrower claim scope, but foreign filings are not permitted until we've satisfied both the university option notice requirement and the technology-control plan. I'd like each of you to confirm your action items so we can lock in the timeline. Elias, can you have the revised claims drafted within the next week? Nina, can you get the option notice requirement on the IP docket today? Owen, can you begin the technology-control plan immediately?
